hero.heading: Odd size, oversize, overweight, or nothing standard about it.
body: Most of what we quote isn't a stock 48×40. It's a skid for a forging that runs nine thousand pounds, a crate for an elevator assembly, cut stock to a rail spec, or a mixed-spec program where four plants each need something different off the same order.

A single mill will usually quote what its equipment likes to build. We start from what the load actually does — weight, whether it's racked or floor-stacked, how many times it gets handled, whether it ships overseas — and then find the shop set up to build it.

whereCustomPays.heading: Where custom usually pays for itself

items.body: Plenty of operations are buying more pallet than the load needs because the spec was set years ago for a heavier product.
Static, dynamic, and racking are three separate load ratings, and the racking number is the one that gets missed.
Multiple specs, staggered releases, several ship-to addresses — the coordination a single mill struggles with is the part we're built for.

ctaBand.heading: Let's talk about your pallet supply.
ctaBand.body: Send a spec and a quantity, or just call and describe the problem.
